analysis.investment_thesis: Cupid Limited is a tiny manufacturer (₹183 Cr revenue) trading at a market cap of ₹13,872 Cr — a P/E of 166x and P/S of 47x for a business growing revenue at just 5.3% CAGR. No quality-conscious value investor can justify this price under any reasonable scenario.
key_strengths: Clean balance sheet with D/E of 0.07 — debt is virtually zero
Healthy gross margins of 62% and operating margins of 35%, suggesting a real niche product with pricing power
Diversified export presence across Africa, Europe, and Asia reduces dependence on domestic demand
key_risks: Valuation is catastrophically detached — P/E 166x vs. 5.3% revenue CAGR; any growth disappointment will destroy the stock
Free cash flow turned deeply negative: -₹31 Cr in 2025 and -₹17 Cr in 2024 despite reported net profit of ₹41 Cr — earnings quality is suspect
Promoter holding at 46%, below my 55% minimum — and 'other income' ballooned to ₹19 Cr in 2025, representing 46% of net profit, masking weak core operating performance
red_flags: P/E of 166x on a ₹183 Cr revenue business is pure speculation, not investing
OCF turned negative (-₹11 Cr) in 2025 while reporting ₹41 Cr net profit — a major divergence signaling working capital deterioration
Balance sheet almost tripled (₹189 Cr → ₹442 Cr) via equity raise, yet revenue grew only ₹27 Cr — capital is not being deployed productively
Other income of ₹19 Cr in 2025 (nearly half of net profit) inflates reported earnings — strip this out and core earnings are far weaker
ROE of 12.9% is below my minimum threshold of 15%, especially alarming after a large equity raise diluting returns
analysis.detailed_analysis:
From my discipline built over decades, I have one simple rule: never pay a price that assumes perfection, because businesses are never perfect. Cupid trades at ₹13,872 Cr market cap on ₹183 Cr in revenue and ₹41 Cr in net profit — that is 75x revenue in real terms and 166x earnings. Even DMart at its most expensive never demanded this faith. The revenue CAGR over four years is a tepid 5.3%, barely above inflation. Operating income CAGR is just 0.6% — essentially flat. This is not a compounder. This is a speculation.

What makes this worse is the cash flow story. A business reporting ₹41 Cr profit but generating negative ₹11 Cr from operations is a business I cannot trust. The equity raise in 2024 added nearly ₹100 Cr in financing inflows and bloated the balance sheet, but revenue barely budged. ₹19 Cr in "other income" in 2025 — nearly half the net profit — raises serious questions about the quality of earnings being reported. The promoter holding of 46% is below my required threshold, and with FII at 1% and DII at 0.17%, this appears to be a retail-driven momentum trade, not an institutional conviction story. I will not participate.
